LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 8.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY:

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.1: Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary:, part of Strand 8 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should you say words clearly? 2. What should you do to say words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. articulate sounds accurately for clarity of speech,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. select sounds correctly from a language sample to improve listening comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use vocabulary items related to the theme in a variety of contexts for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. realise the role of correct pronunciation in speech for communication clarity.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. articulate sounds accurately for clarity of speech,

   Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. select sounds correctly from a language sample to improve listening comprehension,

   Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. use vocabulary items related to the theme in a variety of contexts for effective communication,

   Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. realise the role of correct pronunciation in speech for communication clarity.

   Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. recognise the (sounds /ʊə/ /v/ /w/ /s//ʧ/) from audio materials,

2. articulate vowels and consonants as the teacher models,

3. create a tongue twister using words with the target sounds in small groups,

4. say tongue twisters with the (words containing the sounds /ʊə/ /v/ /w/ /s//ʧ/) individually and collaboratively,

5. select words containing vowels and diphthongs and consonants from a tongue twister, passage, a poem, a song or a story, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. recognise the (sounds /ʊə/ /v/ /w/ /s//ʧ/) from audio materials,
2. articulate vowels and consonants as the teacher models,
3. create a tongue twister using words with the target sounds in small groups,
4. say tongue twisters with the (words containing the sounds /ʊə/ /v/ /w/ /s//ʧ/) individually and collaboratively,
5. select words containing vowels and diphthongs and consonants from a tongue twister, passage, a poem, a song or a story, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary: together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: This is achieved as the learner says the tongue twisters with peers.

Self-efficacy: This is realised as the learner develops know-how on proper enunciation of the targeted sounds.

Values:
Peace: This is enhanced as the learner shows respect for diversity in enunciation of sounds among peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Integration: Ethnic, race and social integration is fostered through group work and video conferencing.

• Health Education: Sensitisation on lifestyle and non-communicable diseases is achieved as the learner learns how to eat

nutritious and healthy meals and how they are grown through the theme of the farm.

Link to other Learning Areas:

A learner can relate the proper articulation of sounds to pronunciation concepts when learning Kiswahili.

Main points to remember:

1. articulate sounds accurately for clarity of speech,
2. select sounds correctly from a language sample to improve listening comprehension,
3. use vocabulary items related to the theme in a variety of contexts for effective communication,
4. realise the role of correct pronunciation in speech for communication clarity.

Remember the key question: Why should you say words clearly? 2. What should you do to say words correctly?
